aliases: Amcrest Smart Home 2K WiFi Video Doorbell AD410

frigate.notes: Uses Dahua protocol (Amcrest standard). Portrait 3:4 aspect ratio — set detect to 720x960. Community favorite for local-only doorbell with Frigate. Button press exposed as Dahua event (AccessControl/CallNoAnswered). go2rtc backchannel (append to the go2rtc stream URL): #backchannel=0 = two-way audio off, normal button/chime behavior (recommended default — go2rtc otherwise auto-opens the Dahua backchannel, which can disrupt the doorbell); #backchannel=1 = two-way audio on, requires extra setup (e.g. github.com/RobTheBuilder2/amcrest-intercom).

home_assistant.notes: Native Amcrest integration. Doorbell button press exposed as 'doorbell' event entity. Two-way audio supported. Also works with ONVIF integration.

blue_iris.notes: Select 'Dahua' profile. Portrait 3:4 aspect ratio. Doorbell press triggers alert.

community_notes.note: go2rtc opens the Dahua two-way-audio backchannel by default, which can disrupt the doorbell's button/chime. Append #backchannel=0 to the go2rtc stream URL for normal behavior; #backchannel=1 enables two-way audio (needs extra setup).

community_notes.note: After a PTZ move command, ONVIF GetStatus reports MoveStatus IDLE for about 0.1 s before switching to MOVING. A client that polls right after the command treats the move as finished, so Frigate autotracking (0.18.2) ends every move at once. Manual PTZ from Frigate works.
ONVIF AbsoluteMove zoom only moves in whole steps of the 4x optical zoom (1x, 2x, 3x, 4x); zoom positions between two steps cannot be reached.

frigate.notes: Portrait 3:4 aspect ratio (white model 1920x2560, black model is 4:3 at 2560x1920). Set detect to 720x960 for white or 960x720 for black to maintain correct ratio. For two-way audio: use go2rtc as the RTSP proxy — Frigate does not natively handle talk-back. In go2rtc config add the camera as an RTSP source, then enable WebRTC with opus re-encoding for the back-channel: 'streams: doorbell: - rtsp://{user}:{pass}@{ip}:554/h264Preview_01_main - ffmpeg:doorbell#audio=opus'. Button press events are not exposed via RTSP; use HA Reolink integration's Visitor binary_sensor or subscribe to ONVIF events via MQTT.

home_assistant.notes: Native Reolink integration auto-discovers via ONVIF (port 8000). Doorbell button press is exposed as a 'Visitor' binary_sensor entity. Two-way audio works in the Reolink app; for HA dashboard intercom, use go2rtc WebRTC card with opus back-channel.

blue_iris.notes: Select 'Reolink' profile. White model is portrait 3:4 — enable 'Rotate 90' or adjust display settings. Doorbell press triggers a motion event.

frigate.notes: go2rtc alternative: TP-Link's proprietary protocol via go2rtc (tapo://<tapo-account-password>@{ip}) is often more stable than RTSP (fewer timeouts / non-monotonic-timestamp errors). The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) — see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker).

The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) — see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). frigate.notes: go2rtc alternative: TP-Link's proprietary protocol via go2rtc (tapo://<tapo-account-password>@{ip}) is often more stable than RTSP (fewer timeouts / non-monotonic-timestamp errors). The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) — see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). Pan/tilt: Tapo exposes ONVIF PTZ on port 2020 (not 80) — point Frigate's onvif block at host:<ip> port:2020 with the camera Account credentials for manual pan/tilt. (Frigate autotracking stays off: Tapo only does continuous-move ONVIF, no reliable absolute/FOV positioning.)

frigate.notes: No native RTSP. Camera and go2rtc must be on the same subnet; internet required at connect time for key exchange. Quality: subtype=hd/sd/auto/0-5. Point Frigate at the go2rtc restream.
